reviewed_candidates.title: Recipe scaling preserves ingredient ratios rather than absolute indexed doses

effective_design.contrast: ratio-preserving scaling versus fixed indexed amounts
effective_design.countermodel: The same surface alternation could reflect editorial batch conventions, lexicalized forms, or analyst counting choices without either proposed semantic rule.
effective_design.falsifier: A matched count change preserves absolute amounts while the source explicitly marks a scaled batch, or ratios vary without a batch/count change.
effective_design.prediction: When product count changes within the same recipe template, ingredient ratios should remain constant under the scaling model; the indexed model predicts stable absolute amounts and changing ratios.
effective_design.principal_risk: Independent product counts and ingredient amounts are unavailable. Near IDEA000049 quantity calibration and old recipe quantity families, but the contrast is transformation across batch size, not unit interpretation or conservation.
effective_design.unit: matched recipe records with an explicit product count and at least two ingredient amounts

reviewed_candidates.logical_assessment: Both a→ka,b→kb and fixeda,b preservea/b. If productcount doubles, scaling predicts absolute amounts double and per-product amount remains fixed; fixedamounts predict absolute quantities unchanged and per-product amounts halve. Draft incorrectly says fixedamounts change ingredient ratios.
reviewed_candidates.specific_missing_observation: No named recipe pair, explicit productcount, two observed amounts, same-unit calibration or known scale factor is supplied. The correct abstract mathematical contrast can be stated without named ingredients, but this is not a manuscript test.
reviewed_candidates.completion_condition: With an actual matched countchange and independently read comparable amounts, test absolute scaling factors or per-product normalization; do not use invariant ingredient ratios alone.

reviewed_candidates.title: Singular and plural marking tracks the counted participant set

effective_design.contrast: participant cardinality agreement versus lexical category marking
effective_design.countermodel: The same surface alternation could reflect editorial batch conventions, lexicalized forms, or analyst counting choices without either proposed semantic rule.
effective_design.falsifier: The form stays fixed when the selected count changes, or switches when only an unselected set changes under matched scope.
effective_design.prediction: Holding lexical category and record type fixed, changing the selected participant count from one to multiple should switch the form; changing an unselected neighboring set should not.
effective_design.principal_risk: Independent participant counts and number meanings are unavailable. Near IDEA000064 argument agreement and historical flower-count material, but targets cardinality of a designated set rather than a modifier’s argument class or a lexical category.
effective_design.unit: records with a counted participant set and a candidate singular/plural form

reviewed_candidates.logical_assessment: Selected-versus-unselected count interaction could be a valid restricted structural hypothesis, but candidate form alternatives, selected set and unaffected neighboring set are unnamed. Generic lexical-category marking can correlate with cardinality unless its conditional rule is fixed.
reviewed_candidates.specific_missing_observation: PHF001 has9owned labels,7singular/2plural, pluralonly2folios;17stable complete literals across24cells havezero repeats. These are actualcount observations but do not fix one lexicalcategory/formpair or selected-versus-neighbor interaction for77.
reviewed_candidates.completion_condition: A nominated form alternation and fixed independently owned selected/unselected count contrast could support a structural number-sensitive rule without known nouns; existing ownership/class/count capacity must first match that unit.

reviewed_candidates.title: A repeated operation is idempotent rather than cumulatively additive

effective_design.countermodel: A context-conditioned lexical convention or editorial repetition could generate the same surface pattern without the proposed operation rule.
effective_design.falsifier: A repeated operation changes the state again under the same input and no intervening operation, or an intervening change is required to produce the observed difference.
effective_design.prediction: When the same operation is repeated without an intervening state change, the second output should equal the first; a cumulative operation should expose a second increment or distinct result marker.
effective_design.principal_risk: Independent operation identity and state measurements are missing. Near quantity scaling and identity persistence, but the discriminator is repeat application under unchanged input.
effective_design.unit: paired records or repeated operation frames with the same input/state

reviewed_candidates.logical_assessment: Idempotence isf(f(s))=f(s), not merely repeatingf(s) from the same reset input. Sequential applications must share operation and tracked participant but second input is first output. A distinct cumulative rival may saturate or have effects below observation resolution.
reviewed_candidates.specific_missing_observation: No named repeated operation, tracked before/after state feature, once-versus-twice matched passage or observation scale is supplied. GDT500 preserves two analyst action slots in15composed German cells; it predicts no manuscript occurrence or output state.
reviewed_candidates.completion_condition: A separately specified state response on actual once/twice serial application could distinguish restricted idempotent/additive models. Repeated tokens, parser normalforms or two clauses alone establish neither repeated physical operation nor state equality.

Status: **STOP — NO TRANSFERABLE FLOWER COUNT AND ZERO EXACT RECURRENCE**.

The human catalogue contains **25** explicit singular/plural flower descriptions: **13 singular** and **12 plural**. **18** have a primary current-locus map. Reusing the frozen ownership audit and reviewing five preselected official-image records yields **9** clear owned flower-count labels: **7 singular** on f88, f89, f100, f102 and **2 plural** on f89, f100. Only f89, f100 mix states. The plural state remains confined to two folios.

Across all **24** clear owned pharmaceutical cells, **17** have one identical complete compact literal surface in ZL3b, IT2a, and RF1b. **None repeats**, within or across folios. A development diagnostic exposed those surfaces after ownership selection, so this is an exploratory zero-recurrence result, not an analyst-blind target test.

No formal root/role or image recognizer was used. This supplies no FLOWER/count word, plant name, sound, language, cipher, plaintext, meaning, or translation.

Das aktuelle deutsche Arbeitsdeck enthält wieder alle 495 Zellen in einer
Ausgabe. Genau fünfzehn komponierte Zellen ändern nur ihre redaktionelle
Oberfläche. Die mechanische Form „Nimm X und nimm X“ oder „Bearbeite X und
bearbeite X“ wird als zweimalige Handlung ausgesprochen:

- `CH+CH`: „Nimm das zuvor Genannte zweimal.“;
- `CHD+CHD+Y`: „Bearbeite den Pflanzenposten zweimal.“;
- `CH+CH+E+Y`: „Nimm den Drogenposten zweimal; auf Grad I.“.

Im celestialen Register bleibt das trennbare Verb natürlich geordnet:
„Nimm den Positionsposten zweimal auf.“ Jede der drei Regeln greift genau
fünfmal, einmal pro Register.

Die fünfzehn Änderungen sind deshalb kein neues Wörterbuch. `zweimal` ist die
knappe deutsche Realisierung der bereits vorhandenen zwei identischen
Handlungsslots.

## Rückführung

Jede geänderte Zeile bewahrt die erste Handlungsklausel, die zweite
Handlungsklausel und ihren Satz- oder Gradabschluss separat. Aus diesen drei
Feldern wird die alte Phrase exakt rekonstruiert. Das gelingt 15/15 Mal; auch
beide technischen Handlungsslots bleiben 15/15 Mal sichtbar. Die neue
Lesefassung kann daher nicht versehentlich aus `CH+CH` nur ein einzelnes CH
machen.
